widgets_values:
FINAL / 3 - HIGH-RES NO-TEAR FLY-THROUGH (no WAN, no splat -- finished frames straight out of MoGe)

360 pano -> MoGe depth -> mesh -> REAL pinhole render at full output resolution. Nothing else in the graph: no WAN, no diffusion, no SfM. It renders in ~0.5s/frame (4K) once MoGe has run (~85s, then cached -- re-render with new anchors is instant).

WHY IT LOOKS BETTER THAN THE WAN CONTROL VIDEO:
  * The control-video path rasterizes 6x 512x512 cube faces and merges them, so detail is capped at ~512px/90deg and the pano is downsized to 2048x1024 first. This node renders pinhole views directly and takes colour per-fragment from the UNTOUCHED full-res panorama. Feed it an 8K pano and a 4K render keeps every pixel of it.
  * The control-video path punches HOLES at depth edges on purpose (that is WAN's inpainting mask). This node closes them instead.

EDGE_MODE -- the actual experiment. Try all four on your pano:
  stretch  = never tears. Rubber-sheet smears at silhouettes only. Cleanest overall on most scenes; start here.
  layered  = re-grows the background behind each silhouette from real pano pixels, then push-pull fills the rest. Sharpest fills, but stair-step artifacts on diagonal edges.
  fill     = just push-pull fill the holes (fast, soft).
  cut      = leave the holes (what the shipping pipeline does) -- use the hole_mask output if you want to inpaint them yourself downstream.

MOVEMENT_SCALE: keep it SMALL (0.05-0.3). Disocclusions grow with parallax and none of these modes can invent geometry that is not in the pano. 0.25 on a 3-anchor path already opens ~19% of the frame.

ANCHORS: same frame/format as Camera Plot -- one 'x,y,z' per line. +Z forward into the pano, +X right, +Y up, origin = start camera. A path tuned in Camera Plot transfers here unchanged.

MESH_WIDTH is GEOMETRY resolution only (texture always comes from the full pano). 2048 is plenty; 4096 sharpens silhouettes at ~2x render cost.

DIRECTIONS (default 6): renders the SAME path once per azimuth, 360/N apart (6 -> every 60 deg). Output is ONE batch of directions x length frames, in order (direction 0 first). Every direction starts at the pano origin and gets its OWN collision guard, so a path that clears a near wall at 0 deg still travels its full length at 180 deg. Watch your VRAM/RAM: 6 x 49 frames at 1920x1080 is ~294 images.

SPIRAL (spiral_radius > 0): the camera orbits up -> left -> down -> right around its line of sight while it flies the path, WITHOUT turning -- it keeps pointing wherever 'orientation' aims it. The circle passes through the start point (frame 0 is exactly the pano origin, the one viewpoint with zero disocclusion) and leaves it heading up. spiral_turns = how many full circles over the path; spiral_phase_deg = which way it sets off (0 up, 90 left, 180 down, 270 right). Radius is in anchor units and is scaled with the path -- 0.05-0.2 is a usable orbit. Combined with directions, this is a cheap way to sweep parallax in every direction for SfM/splat coverage.

hole_mask (preview, right) = WHITE where the render is real geometry, BLACK where the frame was torn open and had to be closed.

Use it to judge how far you can push movement_scale: once the black areas get big, no fill mode will save you -- that is when you go back to the WAN pipeline (workflows/final/1_camera_plot_flythrough.json), which hallucinates the missing content instead of extrapolating it.

In 'cut' mode this mask IS an inpainting mask you can feed to any diffusion inpaint node.
